gallery.source: Sala Royal Albert, Londres, Inglaterra, 2014-08-09, DD 062-64 HDR
gallery.description:
View of the Royal Albert Hall from Prince Consort Road, showing the South Steps and the statue of Prince Consort Albert (work of Joseph Durham in 1858), to whom the hall was honored by his wife, Queen Victoria. The Royal Albert Hall is a concert hall located in South Kensington, London, England. It has a capacity of up to 5,272 seats, and since its opening by Queen Victoria in 1871, world's leading artists from several performance genres have performed there. Each year it hosts more than 350 events including The Proms concerts, that take place annually each summer since 1941.


This is a photo of listed building number 1217742.

gallery.filename: Everything Counts RCA exhibition Routemasters, Royal Albert Hall.jpg
gallery.title: File:Everything Counts RCA exhibition Routemasters, Royal Albert Hall.jpg
gallery.description:
Four Routemaster buses of the Arriva Heritage Fleet, parked up outside the Royal Albert Hall in London. The tape is not the result of an accident, it's there because the four buses have just been used as mobile exhibits for the Everything Counts exhibition, held by the Royal Collage of Art. The installation took place in nearby Exhibition Road from 10am to 6pm, and the buses are now pictured here 45 minutes later outside the hall, presumbaly to be closer to the RCA building, which is out of shot, to the right. From left to right, they are: 
RM2217 (CUV 217C)
RM1124 (124 CLT)
RM6 (VLT 6)
RML901 (WLT 901)
categories: AEC Routemaster buses in the United Kingdom
